response:
Diagnosis. Gen 7 produced a new champion: **Cover And Worst Year Conjunction** — fmb 4.92, alpha 6.1%, ls_talpha 5.41 (the highest reliability in the archive), at *full* coverage 0.145. Three further lessons are now firm. First, the downside-realization operator (worst year of the last five) is genuinely additive information, whereas within-firm *position* is not: Own History Position collapsed to fmb −0.31 with negative alpha, so the market prices the cross-sectional level of true solvency, not a firm's trend relative to itself. Second, conditioning on loss years *narrows* rather than sharpens the evidence (Loss Year Research fell to alpha 2.1%), confirming the critic's mass-point warning. Third, the MAX "fails either test" short-side structure works (fmb −5.29). Since the critic has explicitly ruled that only one conjunction permutation should be carried forward, this generation stops permuting legs: it tests a structurally new bilateral screen, re-specifies which claims actually matter, applies the validated downside operator to a different economic channel, and adds a new fragility channel for the short side.

---SIGNAL 1---
NAME: Bilateral Solvency Minus Fragility Screen
EXPRESSION: SUB(MIN(RANK(RATIO(SUB(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5), COALESCE(gdwl, 0)), lt)), RANK(TS_MIN(RATIO(ADD(ib, COALESCE(xrd, 0)), lt), 5))), MAX(RANK(RATIO(SUB(SUB(DELTA(ceq, 1), ib), COALESCE(xrd, 0)), at)), RANK(RATIO(SUB(COALESCE(gdwl, 0), ADD(ceq, TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5))), lt))))
HYPOTHESIS: A firm's true position is its weakest solvency credential net of its worst fragility flaw: it must pass both solvency tests (real knowledge cover of claims, adequate cover even in its worst year) and fail neither fragility test (dependence on dilution, goodwill exceeding the equity-plus-knowledge cushion).
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: This is not another leg permutation but a different logical object — a conjunction on the long side differenced against a disjunction on the short side — and it is the natural synthesis of the archive's two validated structures, whose components have fmb 4.92 and −5.29 respectively and are constructed from four economically distinct channels (stock cover, downside realization, external financing, impairment overhang). Because the MIN and MAX are taken over cross-sectional ranks, the difference is bounded and symmetric, which should preserve the cross-sectional slope while sharpening both tails rather than thinning them the way a nested triple MIN would.
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel

---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: Persistent Real Knowledge Cover
EXPRESSION: WINSOR(TS_MIN(RATIO(SUB(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5), COALESCE(gdwl, 0)), lt), 5), 1)
HYPOTHESIS: Knowledge cover earned and held for five consecutive years is evidence of a durable business model, while cover that appears only in the current year can be produced by a one-off research burst, a debt paydown, or a goodwill write-off; the minimum cover the firm has sustained is the credible measure.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The worst-year operator delivered real incremental information on the earnings channel, and this asks the sharper question of whether the same downside logic applies to the *stock* channel — durability of the cushion rather than durability of the payment capacity — which is a different economic property and has never been tested here. It is a single continuous, fully covered, monotone level signal, so if it approaches the champion's performance it offers the same evidence without any conjunction machinery, which matters for robustness.
INTERACTION_TYPE: ratio

---SIGNAL 3---
NAME: Knowledge Cover Of Acceleratable Debt
EXPRESSION: WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5), COALESCE(gdwl, 0)), ADD(dltt, dlc)), 1)
HYPOTHESIS: Only financial creditors can accelerate and force default; payables, accruals and deferred items roll with the business, so the economically relevant cover test for a knowledge firm is its real intangible capital per dollar of *acceleratable* debt rather than per dollar of all claims.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The archive's highest-alpha cover ratio divides by total liabilities, which conflates self-liquidating trade credit — a sign of counterparty confidence — with contractual debt that can trigger bankruptcy, and that conflation is a substantive misspecification rather than a scaling preference. Debt-only scaling has been tested with an inferior numerator (alpha 4.9%, t 3.96), so pairing it with the goodwill-netted knowledge stock isolates whether the denominator's claim definition is what has been limiting the family.
INTERACTION_TYPE: ratio

---SIGNAL 4---
NAME: Claims Growth Beyond Knowledge Investment
EXPRESSION: WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(SUB(lt, LAG(lt, 3)), TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 3)), at), 1)
HYPOTHESIS: When a firm's obligations grow by more than everything it invested in research over the same period, the extra claims financed something other than knowledge — losses, acquisitions or working-capital deterioration — and that is the signature of genuine fragility rather than accounting distress.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: This measures the growth of the *entire* claim base, including the operating liabilities that stretch when a firm is running short of cash, which is economically distinct from the debt-issuance and equity-issuance measures already in the archive and not the published net-external-financing anomaly. It gives the short side a channel that does not depend on securities issuance at all, addressing the critic's observation that the current fragility screen leans on a known issuance effect.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 5---
NAME: Worst Year Post Research Margin Cover
EXPRESSION: WINSOR(TS_MIN(RATIO(SUB(SUB(sale, cogs), COALESCE(xrd, 0)), lt), 5), 1)
HYPOTHESIS: The margin a knowledge firm retains after funding the research that sustains it, in the worst year of its recent history, measures the floor of its ability to service claims; firms whose floor is comfortably positive are affordably distressed on paper only.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The downside operator has so far been applied only to bottom-line earnings, which mix in write-downs and one-off items; gross margin net of research is the operating core, so this tests whether the worst-year effect comes from realized operating capacity or from accounting noise in the earnings line. Both parents are strong and full-coverage (post-research margin cover: fmb 3.34, Sharpe 0.253; worst-year earnings cover: fmb 3.07, alpha 4.2%), and the answer determines which numerator the final generation should carry.
INTERACTION_TYPE: ratio

---SIGNAL 6---
NAME: Fails Either Non Issuance Fragility Test
EXPRESSION: MAX(RANK(RATIO(SUB(SUB(lt, LAG(lt, 3)), TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 3)), at)), RANK(RATIO(SUB(COALESCE(gdwl, 0), ADD(ceq, TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5))), lt)))
HYPOTHESIS: Genuine fragility shows up either as obligations growing faster than knowledge investment or as goodwill exceeding the cushion that would absorb its impairment, and a firm exhibiting either is fragile irrespective of whether it has issued securities.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: The validated MAX structure produced the archive's strongest cross-sectional slope, but the critic correctly notes its issuance leg overlaps the published net-equity-issuance anomaly, so replacing that leg with claim-growth-beyond-research tests whether the disjunction's power survives without any issuance information. This is the decisive robustness question for the short side heading into the final generation, and both legs remain genuinely cross-theme with the knowledge stock entering each.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---CRITIQUE Bilateral Solvency Minus Fragility Screen---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: This is essentially the arithmetic difference of two already-evaluated archive signals (the MIN conjunction with fmb 4.92 and the MAX disjunction with fmb −5.29), so a strong result is close to mechanically guaranteed by construction and teaches nothing new about the economics — it is a portfolio blend dressed as a hypothesis, and it re-uses the goodwill/knowledge-stock terms on both sides, partially cancelling them.

---CRITIQUE Persistent Real Knowledge Cover---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: Wrapping the archive's existing cover ratio (xrd5 − gdwl)/lt in TS_MIN is a one-operator cosmetic variant, and because the numerator is itself a five-year cumulative sum of a highly persistent quantity, the five-year minimum is close to a mechanically stale, four-year-lagged version of the parent rather than a genuine "durability" measure.

---CRITIQUE Knowledge Cover Of Acceleratable Debt---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: A pure denominator swap (lt → dltt+dlc) on an existing archive ratio, and the swap introduces a construction problem the reasoning ignores: firms with near-zero financial debt produce explosive or undefined ratios whose cross-sectional ordering is essentially arbitrary, so any apparent gain would be a low-debt-firm artifact rather than evidence about claim definition.

---CRITIQUE Claims Growth Beyond Knowledge Investment---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: With xrd coalesced to zero the signal collapses exactly to three-year liability growth scaled by assets for the large non-R&D majority, making it a direct rediscovery of the well-documented asset/liability-growth and net-operating-liabilities anomalies, and the R&D term is too small relative to Δlt to change the ranking for most firms.

---CRITIQUE Worst Year Post Research Margin Cover---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: It is a crossing of two archive parents rather than a new mechanism, but the diagnostic question it poses — whether the worst-year effect comes from operating capacity or from write-down noise in the bottom line — is well-posed, the expression matches the hypothesis, and coverage should be full.

---CRITIQUE Fails Either Non Issuance Fragility Test---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: The stated robustness motivation is legitimate, but the replacement leg is the same liability-growth construct flagged above as a likely rediscovery of the asset-growth anomaly, so this would substitute one known published effect (net equity issuance) for another rather than establishing that the disjunction survives on genuinely cross-theme information.

---SIGNAL 1---
NAME: True Cushion Survival Horizon
EXPRESSION: WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(ceq, TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5)), ADD(ADD(COALESCE(xrd, 0), MAX(NEG(ib), 0)), dlc)), 1)
HYPOTHESIS: Survival is a question of time, not of coverage ratios: the true equity cushion — book equity plus the unrecorded knowledge stock — divided by the firm's annual cash requirement of research plus current losses plus maturing short-term debt gives the number of years it can continue without new money, and long-horizon firms are only accounting-distressed.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel
REASONING: This abandons the arithmetic blend of two evaluated signals for a genuinely different object — a stock-over-flow measure denominated in years rather than a cover ratio or a rank conjunction — and no archive signal has ever expressed distress as a survival horizon. The denominator deliberately aggregates the three cash demands that actually fall due within a year and is bounded away from zero for any firm with research, losses or maturing debt, so the ordering is well behaved precisely in the distressed region where the measure matters.
REASONING_NOTE_IGNORE: n/a

---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: Revenue Earned Per Dollar Of Burden
EXPRESSION: WINSOR(RATIO(sale, ADD(lt, TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5))), 1)
HYPOTHESIS: A firm that turns over large revenue relative to the sum of what it owes and what it has invested in knowledge is commercially productive and can grow out of apparent distress, while one carrying heavy claims and a heavy research stock against thin revenue has built neither a business nor an asset.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
INTERACTION_TYPE: ratio
REASONING: This replaces the stale-minimum construction with a turnover concept rather than a cover or profitability concept — the archive has tested what a firm owns, what it earns and how it finances itself, but never how much business it transacts per unit of total economic burden. Putting claims and the knowledge stock together in the denominator is what makes it cross-theme and non-mechanical: research-heavy firms are held to a higher revenue standard precisely because their unrecorded capital is large.
REASONING_NOTE_IGNORE: n/a

---SIGNAL 3---
NAME: Acceleratable Debt Share Versus Knowledge Share
EXPRESSION: WINSOR(SUB(RATIO(ADD(dltt, dlc), lt), RATIO(TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5), ADD(lt, TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5)))), 1)
HYPOTHESIS: What endangers a knowledge firm is the mix of its funding: a high share of claims that creditors can accelerate, combined with a low share of its economic position backed by knowledge capital, marks genuine fragility, whereas trade-financed firms with large knowledge stocks are merely distressed on paper.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite
REASONING: Both terms are bounded fractions between zero and one, which eliminates the explosive low-debt ratios the critic identified in the denominator swap while preserving the economic point that only acceleratable debt can force default. It is a composition contrast rather than a rescaled cover ratio: two firms with identical knowledge cover rank very differently depending on whether their claims are contractual debt or self-liquidating trade credit.
REASONING_NOTE_IGNORE: n/a

---SIGNAL 4---
NAME: Claims Against Peak True Capital
EXPRESSION: WINSOR(RATIO(lt, TS_MAX(ADD(at, TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5)), 5)), 1)
HYPOTHESIS: Fragility appears when obligations remain while the capital base that justified them has shrunk; measuring current claims against the largest knowledge-augmented capital base the firm has commanded in five years captures both borrowing that outran investment and capital that has been destroyed by losses or write-downs.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
INTERACTION_TYPE: ratio
REASONING: Anchoring on peak capital rather than on a three-year liability change means the signal is driven as much by shrinkage of the true asset base as by borrowing, so it cannot collapse into the published liability-growth anomaly for non-research firms — and the knowledge stock enters the peak, which is what makes it cross-theme. It is a level ratio with full coverage and no mass point, unlike the differenced construction it replaces.
REASONING_NOTE_IGNORE: n/a

---SIGNAL 5---
NAME: Fails Either Capital Erosion Test
EXPRESSION: MAX(RANK(RATIO(lt, TS_MAX(ADD(at, TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5)), 5))), RANK(RATIO(SUB(COALESCE(gdwl, 0), ADD(ceq, TS_SUM(COALESCE(xrd, 0), 5))), lt)))
HYPOTHESIS: A knowledge firm is genuinely fragile if either its claims now loom large against the best capital base it has ever had, or its acquisition goodwill exceeds the equity-plus-knowledge cushion that an impairment would consume — either condition alone is disqualifying.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional
REASONING: This preserves the validated "fails either test" disjunction while removing every securities-issuance input, so it directly answers whether the structure's power rests on the known net-issuance effect or on genuinely cross-theme information — and unlike the rejected version, the replacement leg is a peak-anchored capital-erosion ratio rather than a liability-growth variable. Both legs embed the knowledge stock, so neither can be reduced to a single-theme published anomaly.
REASONING_NOTE_IGNORE: n/a
